stem: Unexpected delayed reproductive development is seen across several cultivars in the same room. Which shared factor deserves early verification?
choices: Investigate cultivar-specific genetics first because different cultivars can share a delayed phenotype when they are grown under the same room conditions.
Compare nutrient delivery by cultivar because a shared room pattern can still arise from cultivar-specific nutrient demand.
Recalculate the calendar from the schedule change and use days since transition as the primary test of whether the room is truly delayed.
Verify photoperiod/light-dark integrity and other shared room conditions because a multi-cultivar pattern raises the value of checking common exposures.
rationale: When several cultivars in the same room show a similar developmental delay, a shared exposure becomes more plausible than a separate cultivar-specific cause occurring independently in each line. Photoperiod integrity, light leaks or timing errors, temperature, and other room-wide conditions therefore deserve early verification. Genetics and nutrition can still contribute, but the cohort pattern makes a common environmental factor a high-value first check. Calendar counting alone cannot establish whether morphology is abnormal.
